version.changelog:
- Removed all agent configuration and documentation files.
- Updated SKILL.md to limit compliance checks to EU CosIng only; removed support and references to US FDA and China NMPA.
- Streamlined API request and response examples to include only EU market details.
- Updated metadata tags and removed LLM/hallucination language.
- Cleaned up documentation for clarity and focus on EU compliance.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed paid cosmetic compliance API, but its public instructions broaden regulatory scope and payment handling enough that users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: A remote POST endpoint is proportionate for an API-backed compliance lookup, but ingredient lists and payment hashes are sent to a third-party service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only Markdown/text files and no executable installer, dependency, local script, or package-install behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main skill gives EU-focused triggers, but llms.txt uses broader autonomous-agent language and does not clearly constrain unsupported jurisdictions, prohibited uses, or when paid calls should require user approval.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence or privilege escalation is present, but the skill declares x402/Solana payment fields, a recipient wallet, and Authorization-header payment transport without spending limits or explicit human confirmation requirements.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md describes EU CosIng cosmetic compliance checks, while llms.txt advertises EU, US FDA, and China NMPA coverage plus broader e-commerce, chemical, and skincare use cases; that mismatch can lead agents to rely on it outside the declared EU scope.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use a third-party paid Solana/x402 API for cosmetic compliance checks. Require explicit user approval before any payment or payment-hash submission, and treat non-EU claims as unverified unless the publisher documents supported jurisdictions and billing controls more precisely.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: SKILL.md provides EU-focused triggers, but llms.txt is broader and lacks clear boundaries for when autonomous agents should invoke paid compliance checks.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact-backed mismatch is real because SKILL.md declares EU CosIng compliance while llms.txt claims US FDA and China NMPA coverage.
[SDI-2] expected: Downgraded from inherently unrelated to under-scoped: payment is explicitly declared in SKILL.md and llms.txt, but financial authorization controls are not documented.
